Goods can be bought from a single source in the following circumstances:  
(i) When only a particular firm is the manufacturer of the required goods [gfr_2017:R166].  
(ii) In cases of emergency where the required goods must be purchased from a specific source, and the reason is recorded with approval from the competent authority [gfr_2017:R166].  
(iii) For standardisation of machinery or spare parts to be compatible with existing equipment, on the advice of a competent technical expert and with approval from the competent authority [gfr_2017:R166].  
(iv) When there is an urgent need for the work and competitive tendering is impractical, provided the urgency was unforeseeable and not due to the procuring entity's delay [works_manual_2025:3.12].  
(v) When the work represents a natural continuation of previous work by the firm, and the incremental work does not exceed 25% of the original contract value [works_manual_2025:3.12].  
(vi) When execution involves proprietary techniques or only one contractor has the requisite expertise [works_manual_2025:3.12].  
(vii) Under special circumstances where selecting a particular contractor is necessary for the overall interest of the Ministry or Department, with full justification and competent authority approval [works_manual_2025:3.3.3].
